items.headline: Copilot Cowork: A new way of getting work done
items.summary: Microsoft introduces Copilot Cowork, transforming single prompts into multi-step autonomous work across Microsoft 365 apps. The feature handles calendar triage by rescheduling meetings to protect focus time, delegates meeting preparation to generate briefing documents and presentations, and offloads research workflows by organizing findings with citations from web and work sources.

items.headline: Microsoft Build 2026: MAI-Thinking-1 Is First In-House Reasoning Model, Trained Without OpenAI Data
items.summary: Microsoft announced MAI-Code-1-Flash and MAI-Thinking-1 at Build 2026 on June 2, marking its first in-house AI models independent of OpenAI. MAI-Code-1-Flash is a 5-billion parameter coding model achieving 51% on SWE Bench Pro10 while using 60% fewer tokens than comparable models, now rolling out to all GitHub Copilot tiers. This represents Microsoft's strategic shift toward reducing OpenAI reliance and lowering inference costs for enterprise developers.

items.headline: AIR CANADA CHATBOT
items.summary: Air Canada's AI chatbot hallucinated a bereavement refund policy, telling customer Jake Moffatt he could purchase a full-fare ticket and request a discount up to 90 days post-flight when the actual policy required pre-approval. Air Canada argued the chatbot was an independent legal entity responsible for its own actions, but the tribunal ruled the airline was liable for all website information. Air Canada was ordered to pay the promised refund, and the chatbot was quietly removed from the website in April 2024.

The failure mode here is exactly what Phase 5 (Controlled Execution) of our 5-Phase methodology prevents: deploying generative AI without verification workflows or policy alignment checks. items.headline: NIST Launches AI Agent Standards Initiative and Seeks Industry Input
items.summary: NIST announced the AI Agent Standards Initiative in February 2026 through its Center for AI Standards and Innovation to develop voluntary guidelines for autonomous AI agents. The initiative addresses identity and authorization, security and risk management, and monitoring and logging for multi-step AI agents, filling a gap left by existing frameworks designed for prediction-based AI. NIST plans to release an AI Agent Interoperability Profile in Q4 2026, as neither the EU AI Act nor the existing NIST AI RMF adequately address agentic AI systems that take autonomous multi-step actions.
